key_insight: The paper defines a principled notion of "sufficient quantum provenance" by identifying which execution details and recording precision are enough to guarantee a bounded difference between quantum outcome distributions.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum hardware and workflow engineers a certificate for deciding what provenance to keep, at what precision, to support reproducible comparisons without fully simulating outcomes.
method: Uses Hellinger distance as the sufficiency criterion for shared records.
Derives a circuit-level certificate combining channel-mixture noise flags and coherent rotation differences via affinity and fidelity.
Applies the framework to QAOA and hardware measurements to determine minimum record fields and label counts.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 13-bit comparison record keeping Hellinger distance below 0.05 for four-qubit depth-1 QAOA across a noise box, plus archival and hardware evaluations showing a four-field minimum record and task-dependent label counts.
watch_item: The hardware conclusions rely on stationary independent shots, so the guarantees may not extend directly to drift, correlated noise, or changing experimental conditions.
paper_title: Sufficient quantum provenance: retained fields and certified recording precision
